A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RoMA, with matching core methods, figures, and experiments. All 11 pages of v1 and 15 pages of v2 support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains a separate appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original RoMA benchmark results, design ablations, scaling experiments, and efficiency measurements in Tables 2–3 and Figures 1 and 5.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds efficiency, small-object segmentation, foreground-capture, and reconstruction-loss results in Tables 4–8.

M1.justification: Section 5 adds an experimental token-space reconstruction variant using a frozen CLIP teacher and a lightweight MIM head. This is a bounded extension of the training objective; the main Mamba architecture, adaptive rotation strategy, and multiscale pixel-reconstruction loss remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 retains the existing training datasets and AID, UCM, OSCD, and SpaceNetv1 evaluations. It adds iSAID evaluation covering small vehicles, ships, pools, and planes, and extends efficiency testing to 4096×4096 inputs. Coverage expands within optical remote sensing; SAR and hyperspectral evaluation remain future work.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains its comparator set. The new iSAID comparison reports additional backbones including IMP-ResNet-50, RSP-ResNet-50, ViTAE-B+RVSA, and RingMo. Table 7 also introduces a quantitative random-cropping comparator for adaptive region selection.

E3.justification: Existing pretraining and main benchmark settings remain unchanged. Added protocols include A100 efficiency measurements with batch size 1, iSAID fine-tuning following RingMo settings, and foreground-capture measurement. The A100 results are separate from Figure 1's retained batch-size-2 experiment and do not establish same-setting performance changes.

E4.justification: Beyond retaining Table 3's ablations, v2 adds a substantial analysis section testing ultra-high-resolution scalability, small-object performance, adaptive versus random foreground capture, and pixel-space versus token-space reconstruction. These provide additional tests of the framework's scalability, selection mechanism, and objective flexibility.

E5.justification: Figure 5 newly reports averages over three experiments and displays 95% confidence intervals. v1 gives neither run counts nor uncertainty intervals for these scaling curves. This is newly documented statistical reporting, not evidence that the run count increased from a known v1 setting.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 retain their scores, but Tables 4–8 add substantial results. These include RoMA operating at 4096×4096 while ViT is out of memory from 2048×2048, iSAID mIoU of 67.4 versus RingMo's 67.2, and foreground capture of 75.09% versus random cropping's 38.56%. Table 8 reports token-space scores of 56.67/81.72 versus pixel-space scores of 52.39/80.34 on UCM-55/AID-55. These are new comparisons, not improvements over matched v1 experiments.

T1.justification: The autoregressive factorization and multiscale MSE objective remain mathematically unchanged: v1 Equations 1 and 5 correspond to v2 Equations 1 and 2. The rotation-selection equations are recast as procedural explanations rather than replaced by a substantively different mathematical argument. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace claims of object-detection evaluation with change-detection evaluation, matching the retained experiments. The conclusion also drops v1's inconsistent 6.25M-to-400M data-scaling range. The central novelty, scaling, and efficiency claims remain substantially the same.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking cropping to small-object visibility and token-space supervision to stronger semantic representations, plus an explicit optical-imagery limitation. It also introduces inconsistencies: Section 3.2.2 disclaims explicit angle prediction despite retained introductory wording, and Table 3e describes sparsity regularization although the objective still combines two reconstruction losses.

D1.justification: The abstract changes code and model availability from a planned release to a reported release at the same RoMA link. v2 adds CLIP-teacher and MIM-head information, new experiment hardware settings, and more explicit cropping instructions. Figure 1's GPU designation changes from 4090PLUS to 4090; the PDFs do not establish a rerun.

R1.justification: Related work expands to ReDet, CSL, S2A-Net, CROMA, and AnySat, and the new loss experiment cites CAE and CLIP. RVSA receives additional discussion, while the MAP comparison is removed. The overall positioning as autoregressive Mamba pretraining for remote sensing remains intact.

P1.justification: v2 reorganizes the autoregressive motivation into the RoMA section, rewrites cropping equations as numbered steps, and simplifies related-work and experimental subheadings. It adds Further Analyses and a brief limitations statement, and revises author information. Much of the introduction, core method description, and existing experimental discussion remains closely matched.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column to a single-column layout, substantially resizing and repositioning existing displays. Figure 5 is rearranged and gains confidence-interval bars, while five new tables present the additional analyses. Existing diagrams and Tables 1–3 are largely retained, with caption and formatting revisions.

improvement.justification: The new high-resolution tests, small-object evaluation, and foreground-capture comparison strengthen evidence for RoMA's central motivations, while Figure 5 makes scaling uncertainty visible. These gains are limited by sparse protocol details for the new studies and inconsistent explanations of angle prediction and the loss coefficient. Overall, v2 provides better empirical support but leaves important clarity and reproducibility gaps unresolved.
